outcome.ru: Риск многосистемной иммунной дисрегуляции (≥2 подсистем) к концу миссии
outcome.en: Risk of multi-system immune dysregulation (≥2 subsystems) by the end of the mission
outcome.definition: Two or more of four subsystems involved: inflammation, leukocyte shift, EBV reactivation, stress axis. Study grading: 0 — no changes, 1 — one subsystem, 2 — two subsystems or a clinical manifestation, 3 — systemic dysregulation.

intercept.why: Not fitted. Derived from the assumption q = 0.15 (0.07–0.3): the share of subsystems that become involved by month 6 in a person who is stable early in flight. For two of four subsystems this gives ~11% (90%: ~3–35%). Shifts usually appear in the first weeks and persist (Crucian 2014, 2015), so stable markers are a good sign; late changes are still possible: in a year of isolation immune responses intensified after 3–4 months (Feuerecker 2019).

dysregulation_score.why: Not fitted. Follows from the outcome definition: with 1 involved subsystem one more is needed (~39% at q = 0.15); with 2 the outcome is already met (90%, allowing for a one-off outlier). The slope is the line through these three points.

duration_log2.why: Not fitted. Rooney 2019: viral shedding on short flights (10–16 days) vs the ISS (≥180 days): any herpesvirus 53→61%, VZV 41→65%, EBV 82→96%, CMV 47→61%. Per doubling of mission length the log-odds rise by 0.09, 0.27, 0.45, 0.15; the median 0.21 is used. The risk grows with mission length, but ever more slowly: most shifts appear early in flight.

method: Knowledge-based model: parameters come from published studies and explicit assumptions (training/config.py), no fitting; the interval reflects the uncertainty of these assumptions and widens further beyond the longest spaceflight.

cytokine.why: Systemic inflammation. After flight IL-6 rises together with IL-10, CRP and MCP-1, as in astronauts after long missions (Kim 2024); cytokine shifts persist throughout flight (Crucian 2014). Absolute threshold 7 pg/mL: 95th percentile of 817 healthy adults (Elecsys IL-6). Relative threshold +71% = reference change value (RCV) for a within-person IL-6 variability of 30–48%; 27% in the Inspiration4 crew over three pre-flight draws (NASA OSDR, OSD-575).

immune_shift.why: NLR rises in flight (Paul 2020), but the marker is non-specific (acute stress, sampling time); upper reference limit 3.53 (Forget 2017). Relative threshold +46% (RCV): the assumed NLR variability of ≈20% matched the one measured in the Inspiration4 crew over three pre-flight draws (training/checks.py). Lower weight: in all studies with an isolated leukocyte shift the outcome was mild.

viral.why: A direct sign of lost T-cell control over latent viruses, the link closest to clinical events (Mehta 2017; Crucian 2018). Threshold ≈129 copies/mL: geometric midpoint between the pre-flight level (40) and the in-flight mean (417) in Pierson 2005 (32 astronauts, 1398 saliva samples).

neuroendocrine.why: Stress hormones trigger EBV reactivation: cortisol (Stowe 2000), catecholamines (Stowe 2001); on the ISS reactivation coincided with a shift in the daily cortisol rhythm (Mehta 2017). Relative threshold +39% = RCV for a cortisol CVi of 16% (15–21% across EFLM database versions, giving +37…+50%). Absolute threshold 550 nmol/L is the team's benchmark (near the upper limit of the morning reference interval; method-dependent).

cortisol_bv.citation: EFLM Biological Variation Database, cortisol (serum, morning): median CVi ≈ 16%; 15.2% and 20.9% in versions of the Ricós/Westgard database.

crucian2014.citation: Crucian BE, et al. Plasma cytokine concentrations indicate that in vivo hormonal regulation of immunity is altered during long-duration spaceflight. J Interferon Cytokine Res. 2014;34(10):778-786.

crucian2015.citation: Crucian B, et al. Alterations in adaptive immunity persist during long-duration spaceflight. NPJ Microgravity. 2015;1:15013.

crucian2018.citation: Crucian BE, et al. Immune system dysregulation during spaceflight: potential countermeasures for deep space exploration missions. Front Immunol. 2018;9:1437.

elecsys_il6.citation: Roche Diagnostics. Elecsys IL-6: upper reference limit 7 pg/mL (95th percentile, 817 apparently healthy individuals), method sheet.

feuerecker2019.citation: Feuerecker M, et al. Immune sensitization during 1 year in the Antarctic high-altitude Concordia environment. Allergy. 2019;74(1):64-77.

forget2017.citation: Forget P, et al. What is the normal value of the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio? BMC Res Notes. 2017;10:12.

fraser2001.citation: Fraser CG. Biological Variation: From Principles to Practice. Washington, DC: AACC Press; 2001 (reference change value, RCV = √2·z·√(CVa² + CVi²)).

garrett2019.citation: Garrett-Bakelman FE, et al. The NASA Twins Study: a multidimensional analysis of a year-long human spaceflight. Science. 2019;364(6436):eaau8650.

il6_bv.citation: Cava F, et al. Biological variation of interleukin 6 (IL-6) and soluble interleukin 2 receptor (sIL2R) in serum of healthy individuals (2000): CVi ≈ 48%; Dugué B, Leppänen E.: CVi ≈ 30%; within-person variability of IL-6 in healthy people is 30–48%.

kim2024.citation: Kim J, et al. Single-cell multi-ome and immune profiles of the Inspiration4 crew reveal conserved, cell-type, and sex-specific responses to spaceflight. Nat Commun. 2024;15:4954. Crew tests: NASA OSDR OSD-569 (complete blood count), OSD-575 (serum cytokines).

leuko_bv.citation: Delanghe JR, et al. (editorial on leukocyte-ratio biomarkers): CVi neutrophils 16.1%, lymphocytes 10.4%; CV of a ratio ≈ √(CV₁² + CV₂²).

manzey1998.citation: Manzey D, Lorenz B, Poljakov V. Mental performance in extreme environments: results from a performance monitoring study during a 438-day spaceflight. Ergonomics. 1998;41(4):537-559.

mehta2017.citation: Mehta SK, et al. Latent virus reactivation in astronauts on the International Space Station. NPJ Microgravity. 2017;3:11.

nasa_std3001.citation: NASA OCHMO. Radiation protection technical brief (NASA-STD-3001): career limit 600 mSv effective dose. ISS dose rate ~0.2–0.5 mSv/day: Simonsen L., NASA NTRS 20250006168.

paul2020.citation: Paul AM, et al. Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio: a biomarker to monitor the immune status of astronauts. Front Immunol. 2020;11:564950.

pierson2005.citation: Pierson DL, Stowe RP, Phillips TM, Lugg DJ, Mehta SK. Epstein-Barr virus shedding by astronauts during space flight. Brain Behav Immun. 2005;19(3):235-242.

rooney2019.citation: Rooney BV, Crucian BE, Pierson DL, Laudenslager ML, Mehta SK. Herpes virus reactivation in astronauts during spaceflight and its application on Earth. Front Microbiol. 2019;10:16.

stowe2000.citation: Stowe RP, et al. Stress-induced reactivation of Epstein-Barr virus in astronauts. Neuroimmunomodulation. 2000;8(2).

stowe2001.citation: Stowe RP, Pierson DL, Barrett AD. Elevated stress hormone levels relate to Epstein-Barr virus reactivation in astronauts. Psychosom Med. 2001;63(6):891-895.

zeitlin2013.citation: Zeitlin C, et al. Measurements of energetic particle radiation in transit to Mars on the Mars Science Laboratory. Science. 2013;340(6136):1080-1084.

validation.scheme: not applicable: no independent outcome data
validation.reason: In aggregated_dataset.csv the outcome equals the sum of the input flags in 37 of 41 rows (target leakage), so accuracy metrics on it are not informative.
